list.heading: Remote servers
list.subtitle: The servers you migrate accounts from. The panel reaches each one over SSH with a key it generates for that server alone.
list.emptyDescription: Add the server you want to migrate from. The panel generates a key for it and shows you the one line to put on that server.
list.noResultsDescription: Change the search or the filter, or clear them to see every server.

form.subtitleNew: Tell the panel where the server is. It then generates a key for it and reads the server's host keys.
form.subtitleEdit: Change how the panel reaches the server.
form.notFoundDescription: This remote server does not exist, or it was removed.

fields.name: Name
fields.allowedFrom: Limit the key to these addresses

hints.name: A name only you see, unique among the remote servers.
hints.host: A name or an address the panel can reach. Private and loopback addresses of this host are refused.
hints.sshUser: The panel connects as this user. Root sees every account; another user sees only what it can read.
hints.allowedFrom: Optional. Addresses or ranges separated by commas. They go in front of the key on the server, so only this panel's address can use it.
hints.retarget: Changing the host, the port or the login forgets the confirmed host key. You confirm it again.

errors.hostRequired: Enter the host name or address.
errors.hostInvalid: Enter a host name or an IP address without spaces or a scheme.
errors.portInvalid: The port is a whole number from 1 to 65535.
errors.sshUserRequired: Enter the login on the server.
errors.sshUserInvalid: A login starts with a lowercase letter or an underscore and holds lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores.
errors.allowedFromInvalid: Enter addresses or ranges such as 203.0.113.10 or 10.0.0.0/8, separated by commas.

form.created: The server {name} was added. Put its key on the server, then confirm the host key.

detail.heading: Remote server
detail.subtitle: How the panel reaches this server, and what it found there.
detail.notFoundDescription: This remote server does not exist, or it was removed.

key.title: Authorize the panel on the server
key.intro: Add this one line to the login's authorized keys on the remote server. The matching private key never leaves this panel and is not shown anywhere.

steps.open: Sign in to the remote server as the login you entered.
steps.append: Append the line below to the file ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of that login (create the file with mode 600 if it does not exist).
steps.test: Come back here, confirm the host key, and test the connection.

key.limit: This key cannot be limited to read-only. The restrictions in the line stop forwarding and terminals, but whoever holds the key can run commands as that login. The panel itself only reads. Remove the line when the migration is finished.
key.notLimitedFrom: The key is not limited to any address.

hostKey.title: Confirm the host key
hostKey.intro: The panel read these host keys from the server. Check one against the server itself, so you know you reach the machine you mean and not an impostor.
hostKey.compare: On the remote server run ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub (or the file of the algorithm you choose) and compare the fingerprint it prints with the one you pick below.
hostKey.typeLabel: Type or paste the fingerprint you chose
hostKey.typeHint: The confirm button stays off until what you typed is exactly the chosen fingerprint.
hostKey.mismatch: This is not the chosen fingerprint.
hostKey.noCandidates: The panel holds no scanned host key for this server. Scan again.
hostKey.changedWarning: The server now presents a different host key than the one you confirmed. This can be a reinstall of the server, or someone standing between the panel and the server. Do not confirm a new key unless you know why it changed.

test.title: Connection
test.needsKey: Confirm the host key before the connection can be tested.

failure.hostKeyChanged: The server presented a different host key than the one you confirmed.
failure.authRefused: The server refused the panel's key. Check that the line is in the right authorized_keys file and that the login is correct.
failure.unreachable: The server could not be reached. Check the address, the port and any firewall in front of it.
failure.addressRefused: The panel refuses to connect to this address (a loopback, link-local or own address).

facts.title: What the panel found
facts.loginUser: not root, sees only what it can read
facts.mailFound: Mail storage found. Mail is not migrated.

accounts.title: Accounts on the server
accounts.subtitle: What discovery found. Discovery only reads; nothing on the remote server changes.
accounts.needsPin: Confirm the host key before the panel can read the server.
accounts.neverDiscoveredDescription: Discovery reads the accounts, sites, databases and cron entries from the server.
accounts.noneFoundDescription: Discovery found no account with a home under /home on this server.
accounts.noResultsDescription: Change the search or the filter, or clear them to see every account.
accounts.warningsSubtitle: These items are skipped or incomplete. They do not stop the rest.

account.title: Account {name}
account.noSites: No sites were found for this account.
account.noDatabases: No databases were found for this account.
account.loadFailed: The account could not be read.

remove.confirmQuestion: The panel forgets the server, its confirmed host key and everything discovered on it. Nothing on the remote server changes, so its authorized_keys still holds the panel's key until you remove it yourself.
remove.reminderIntro: The server is removed from the panel. Now take the panel's key off the remote server, so it can no longer be used to sign in:
remove.reminderStep: Delete the line holding this key from ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of the login the panel used.
remove.fingerprint: The host key that was confirmed: {fingerprint}
